detection.note: TypeScript rebuild on Next.js App Router, Postgres with Drizzle, tenant isolation by Postgres row-level security, Better Auth with admin-provisioned accounts, deployed as app-and-database on one small AWS instance with direct connections so RLS session variables behave. Decided against the Laravel-and-Filament recommendation still standing in docs/specs/01-tech-stack.md; that document records the predecessor's fingerprint, not this decision. The lint and test commands still point at the shell gates only: aiming them at npm scripts before a package.json exists would fail every stage for reasons unrelated to the change under review, so they flip when the walking skeleton lands.

tier1.name: low
tier1.description: Documentation, markdown, changelogs, and non-code config changes

tier2.name: medium
tier2.description: Application source, tests, and build configuration

tier3.name: high
tier3.description: Tenant isolation, authorisation, flight-log parsing, schema migrations, and the extracted contracts. Getting these wrong is either a cross-tenant data breach or a corruption of the airworthiness record. Tier 3 no longer gates on human approval - the owner granted the agent loop full merge authority - so the review agent and the full check set are the only things standing here. The one exception is contracts/**: it is the test oracle, it is listed in protected_files, and an agent that can weaken an assertion can make every gate report green while the behaviour is wrong.

shaDiscipline.description: All CI gates pin to exact commit SHA from the risk policy gate
